technical_and_design_decisions: Maintain backward compatibility with existing Spring XD module APIs when migrating kafka, rabbit, and header-enricher modules to avoid breaking changes for existing users.
Implement a common Binder SPI using the strategy pattern to abstract binder-specific operations, enabling pluggable support for kafka, rabbit, and redis binders without modifying core module logic.

Leverage Spring's native externalized configuration support (property files, YAML, environment variables) for the external config override feature, including support for overriding Maven coordinates via standard Spring configuration properties.

Preserve the existing Cloud Foundry Cloud Controller (CC) SPI interface when refactoring the deployer to use the official Cloud Foundry Java Client, ensuring no breaking changes for existing deployer implementations.

Implement a pluggable Hadoop distribution loader interface with default adapters for Apache, Cloudera, and Hortonworks distributions, allowing users to select their preferred distribution via external configuration.

Follow Spring's official dependency upgrade guidelines for the Spring 4.2.1, Spring Integration 4.2, and AMQP 1.5 upgrade, including updating all incompatible transitive dependencies and running full regression tests.
Align the new Binder SPI design with existing Spring Cloud Stream binder patterns to minimize the learning curve for s-c-s developers.
assumptions: The existing Spring XD and s-c-s repositories are accessible with appropriate write permissions for migrating modules.
Existing unit and integration tests for the kafka, rabbit, and header-enricher modules are available and can be executed in the target repository environments.
The selected version of the Cloud Foundry Java Client is fully compatible with the Spring 4.2.1 runtime used in the project.
All required Hadoop distribution native library artifacts are available in public Maven repositories, with no need for custom local builds.
There are no unreleased breaking changes in Spring Integration 4.2, Spring 4.2.1, or AMQP 1.5 that would require extensive rewrites of existing module code beyond standard upgrade procedures.

The external config override feature will support standard Spring configuration file formats (properties, YAML) and environment variables, with override priority following Spring's standard configuration precedence rules.
The binder type selection for module channels will be configured via a single top-level Spring property, with no required changes to existing module application code.
